I released A and the outage is over, but I stopped before B2 and C2: Sveltos is being refused by the admission policy on the management cluster, which is the stop condition you set.

## What was released

| Order | Release | Published (UTC) | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| A `outage-2-a-take-over-shop-lockdown` | `e05ea033-4d0c-4c0c-b52e-3dfc66276611` | 16:15:16 | published, applied by Sveltos from 16:16:10 |
| B2 `outage-2-b2-profiles-only-from-record` | none | not published | held |
| C2 `outage-2-c2-remove-shop-lockdown` | none | not published | held |

I ran the publish as worker `angel`. The release record ConfigHub shows me (tag `outage-2-a-take-over-shop-lockdown-co-end`) has no publisher field, so I cannot quote ConfigHub's own attribution. The aborted orders were not touched.

## Recovery times (UTC)

| Cluster | NetworkPolicy `lockdown` gone | web 2/2 | Live status Healthy |
|---|---|---|---|
| prod-us-1 | by 16:16:13 | by 16:16:19 | observed 16:16:51 |
| prod-us-2 | by 16:16:16 | by 16:16:16 | observed 16:16:32 |

- **How these were taken:** the cluster times are when my poll first saw the change, so the real moment is a few seconds earlier.
- **Staging and prod-eu:** both stayed Healthy throughout, and the `chaos-shop` health check is true on all four clusters as of 16:16:47.

## What was unexpected

- **A stray binding exists.** A ValidatingAdmissionPolicyBinding `profiles-only-from-record` (action Deny) was already on the management cluster, created 15:32:26 by `kubectl-client-side-apply`. It did not come from the record, and I do not know who applied it. The policy itself was hand-applied at the same second.
- **A's policy is therefore enforcing.** A was meant to carry the policy unbound. With the binding present it denies, and A's version exempts `register-mgmt-cluster`, while Sveltos writes as `system:serviceaccount:projectsveltos:projectsveltos`.
- **Sveltos is refused on every ClusterProfile in the record.** That is all eight shop and platform profiles plus `shop-lockdown`. The live status for `chaos-management` is OutOfSync / Degraded / Failed, with the message "ClusterProfile shop-staging may not be written by system:serviceaccount:projectsveltos:projectsveltos".
- **The outage ended anyway.** The ConfigMap `default/shop-lockdown` is not covered by the policy, so A emptied it and Sveltos withdrew the NetworkPolicy.
- **The `shop-lockdown` ClusterProfile is not taken over.** It still has its hand-applied spec. It is harmless while the ConfigMap stays empty.
- **Fleet delivery is not affected for now.** The per-cluster profiles already exist and pull their own variants. What is blocked is any change to the profiles in the record.
- **Waiting.** Foreground `sleep` is blocked in this session, so I waited by repeating read commands instead.

## Decision for you

B2 changes the exemption to `projectsveltos:projectsveltos`, the identity named in the refusal, and brings the binding into the record, so publishing it would probably clear the refusal. I did not publish it because your approval assumed the policy was enforcing nothing until B2, and it is not.

If you tell me to go ahead, I will publish B2, confirm the refusal clears and the record's profiles are unchanged, and only then publish C2. If you would rather the hand-applied binding be explained or removed first, that is outside what I may do with kubectl.
